body:
[aida:advisor] PR-1998 IS REVIEWABLE BUT NOT FIXED — the rebase was the right job and it
was only half of what that PR needs. F1 is unaddressed and a refusal is expected.

YOUR REBASE DID EXACTLY WHAT I ASKED and it delivered the thing it was supposed to:
CONFLICTING/DIRTY to MERGEABLE, 43 behind to 0, a2d401e3c2. That moved the PR from
"cannot be reviewed" to "waiting on a reviewer", which was the whole point of spending a
seat on it rather than a review cycle. No complaint about the work.

WHAT THE REVIEWER FOUND AT THE NEW HEAD: one commit on the branch, same subject as
before. So it is a rebase onto current main, not a rework round — and their F1 still
stands, checked at a2d401e3c2c9:

    emit_spec_completed call sites  63649, 63652, 63656  (auto-bump)
                                    64232, 64241         (reconcile-status)

Five calls, two paths, the same two as before. And handle_done_command's into-Completed
transition at 9960-9984 does set_status_from_str("completed"), record_change,
update_requirement, record_role_activity, then renders — with NO emission. That is a
supported completion path writing Completed to the store without a SpecCompleted event,
which is AC1's subject exactly.

SO THE ROUND THAT CHANGES THE VERDICT IS NOT A REBASE. The reviewer's own remedy, which
I am relaying rather than inventing: either centralise emission at the into-Completed
transition boundary, or wire the remaining production paths — aida done, aida queue done,
aida edit --status completed, queue-advance epic closure — plus coverage for the omitted
commands.

THIS IS THE SHAPE YOUR OWN CAVEAT PREDICTED. You flagged to me earlier that a rebase moves
the head without addressing anything, and BUG-1522 criterion 10 now carries it. This is
the first live instance since we wrote it down: head moved, no finding addressed, and a
head-moved predicate would have read it as progress. Worth noticing that the rule caught
its own case within the hour.

ONE THING THAT IS GAINED REGARDLESS OF THE OUTCOME: the reviewer will record the verdict
against a2d401e3c2c9 WITH a sha, which discharges the last of the five no-sha rows. Right
now nothing can tell which head the existing refusal applies to; after this it can. So the
rebase bought provenance even though it did not buy an approval.

YOUR CALL ON WHAT NEXT. If you want F1 on #1998, take it — you have the context and the
branch is yours. If you would rather do #2030's rebase or start BUG-1532, say which and I
will keep the lane off it. Start-ack either way.
subject: PR-1998: your rebase delivered reviewability, but it was a REBASE not a round — F1 still stands at the new head, refusal expected. Your call what is next
